# ARGUS 2027 build progress

The build session's log. Feature and gate status live in `docs/build/features.json`; read them with `python3 tools/build_ledger.py summary`. The live copies of both files are on the integration branch `platform/build-2027`; `main` keeps the starting copies until the build ends. How the session works is in `docs/build/SESSION.md`.

## Needs a person

Steps the session cannot do. The session adds a row whenever a feature leaves one.

It would earn its place only if the aircraft, holding on the retune alone in a steady wind, sits downwind of the target by more than the gusts move it: fly that hold first (the hold's median error and its direction against the wind's). The pilot's throttle stick stays at its middle during autonomous flight: in LOITER the stick is the climb rate, and a stick resting low brings the vehicle down. ## Decisions made during the build

Choices the specs did not settle, with the reason. Newest first.

| Date | Feature | Decision | Why |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 2026-11-25 | CEN-07 | Three more rules on the wind compensation, from the reviews: the command sent is held to the controller's own slew limit (0.5 m/s in a second), the two terms included; nothing is learnt on a tick whose track is not CONFIRMED (the error to a remembered track is not the wind's) or after a mode that is not GUIDED (the vehicle's velocity is then somebody else's); and what was learnt is dropped after three ticks (0.15 s) without a step, where the controller itself waits half a second. | The spec gives CEN-02's slew limit for the command and says nothing of the wind's terms; the others are the flight reviewer's concerns, taken the careful way. |
| 2026-11-24 | CEN-07 | Wind compensation is `drone_mission_core/wind_compensation.py`, behind the mission flag `wind_compensation` (needs `centring_retune`), applied to the retuned controller's command: an observer of the push (the vehicle's reported velocity less what was commanded 0.4 s before, low-passed over 3 s, limited to 0.8 m/s) taken off the command, and an integral of the error (0.10 per second, limited to 0.5 m/s) summed only within 0.6 m of the target, while the vehicle moves slower than 0.2 m/s, and while the command is under its cap. The sum is held to the controller's own speed cap, which is not raised for the wind; both terms start from nothing when the target is lost. | The spec names an integral term and a disturbance observer from commanded against achieved velocity and gives no numbers. The three conditions on the integral came from the loop simulator: without them a capped approach against the wind arrived with the integral full and sat half a metre past the target, and a plain step overshot 0.18 m. |
| 2026-11-24 | OPS-07 | The rig's analysis is `tools/impulse_rig.py`: from each set-down's recording, the impulse (the integral of force over the package's settled weight from the touch to rest, which is the package's momentum), the peak force and the contact time; across trials, straight lines through zero against descent speed, and with a limit the fastest descent under it by the worst trial with a fifth in hand. A limit is taken as an impulse or as a peak force. A recording with under 8 samples in the contact is refused. The rig and the procedure are `docs/ops/impulse_rig.md`. The row is PARTIAL: there is no rig. Only a load cell's recording is read: an accelerometer on a free plate (the spec's other option) starts and ends at rest, so its acceleration sums to nothing over the touch and never shows the package's weight; reading it needs an analysis of its own, which is not built (found by the spec audit: the first version multiplied acceleration by the plate's mass, which no real recording would have survived). A set-down in which nothing knocks (the vehicle holds the package until it stands) gives no slope against speed: the tool then says the limit bounds no speed at the speeds tried, instead of a speed. | The organisers have said neither the limit nor how they measure it (question 9), and the two readings differ: the impulse depends on mass and speed only, the peak also on how hard the surfaces are. Having both ready costs nothing. The worst trial, not the mean, because one hard set-down is what would be penalised. |
| 2026-11-24 | OPS-05 | The slot clock is `tools/slot_clock.py` with its budget in `tools/slot_clock.yaml`: a slot of 20 min cut into setup 4, preflight 2, flight 10 and pack-up 4, and the list due 30 min after the slot. The slot's length and the phases are the session's working values. The clock is the computer's own time against a start that is given on each machine (the laptop's `start` prints the command for the aircraft); nothing is sent over the link. The GO launcher prints the line before the preflight and at GO and warns when less of the slot is left than a flight and its pack-up; it never refuses a flight for the clock. 'On the ground station' is `show --watch` in a terminal on the laptop. The start crosses to the aircraft as an instant with its zone (the command `start` prints carries an ISO time), because the two computers' clocks are made to agree (PLT-13) and their zones are not; a start with no zone in the file is not a running slot. The launcher takes the budget file as an argument, so its tests count against a budget of their own and the committed one is the lead's to change. | The spec asks for a timeline shown by the launcher and on the ground station and gives no lengths (organiser question 2 is open). Both machines already share a clock (PLT-13), so a start time is all that has to cross. Whether to fly with little of the slot left is a judgement about points, which is the lead's, so the clock tells and does not stop. |
| 2026-11-24 | PLT-14 | The ground station's tools are `tools/judges_list_view.py` (the list as a table, what is wrong with it, a one-file map, the difference from an earlier list), `tools/attempt_download.py` (rsync over ssh, the list first on request, every file checked against the bundle's manifest) and `tools/ground_station.sh`, which runs any of the repo's tools, or a ROS command, in the sim's Humble image on a Jazzy laptop. QGroundControl's setup is a document (`docs/ops/ground_station.md`), and QGroundControl itself runs on the laptop, not in the container. The bundle download does not run in the container either, against the spec's 'all in the Humble container': the image has no ssh and no rsync (run and seen), and the download needs the laptop's own keys and known hosts; the wrapper runs it with the laptop's python3 (it is standard library only). The viewer treats an ID as one digit and holds places against the site file's survey area. | The spec lists QGroundControl setup, a list viewer and bundle download in the Humble container. The Python tools have no ROS in them, so the container is for sameness across laptops and for ROS's own tools on a bag; the image the sim already builds is that container, and a second image would be one more thing to keep. The session has no QGroundControl to make a settings file with. |
| 2026-11-24 | PLT-11 | The health monitor is a node of its own, `health_monitor` (drone_utils), behind `features.health_monitor` and started only when asked, like the other 2027 nodes. It counts the messages of the topics it is told (raw: nothing is decoded), reads the kernel's thermal zones, whether a CPU's allowed top frequency is under what it can do (throttling), the CPUs' busy share and, where the kernel gives it, the GPU's load (the Jetson's file; 'not known' elsewhere), and the frame counts a node says of itself (`/loc/status`). A condition is a finding after five seconds and over five seconds after it stops. Findings go to the ground station as STATUSTEXT through MAVROS, one line at a time, two seconds apart, again every thirty seconds while they last, and `ARGUS H:OK` once when the last has gone: `ARGUS H:RATE/SILENT/TEMP/THROTTLE/CPU/GPU/DROP ...`, within 50 characters. Limits: a rate under four fifths of what is expected, 3 s silent, 85 C, CPU 95%, GPU 98%, a tenth of a node's frames dropped. It tells and commands nothing. It says one line when it starts watching (`ARGUS H:ON`), so that silence afterwards is 'nothing wrong' and not 'no monitor'. Only a node that publishes its own frame counts is watched for drops: the grabbers and the detector do not, and theirs are not watched. The sim's shipped list has the camera only: the pose comes at 30 a second only with the stream keeper running, and without it a flight would be warned about from start to end. The scenario builder gained `node_params`: a scenario may give a node other values for parameters the shipped params file already holds, with its flags on. | The spec: rates, temperatures and throttling, CPU and GPU load, dropped frames; short STATUSTEXT codes to QGroundControl. The numbers are the session's. Thirty seconds between repeats and two between lines keep the link for the flight controller's own messages. |
| 2026-11-24 | LOC-12 | The pass after landing is a tool, `tools/second_pass.py`, run by a person on the aircraft's computer once the localisation node is stopped; the node does not run it. With the node flag `features.post_landing_pass` on (it needs the frame log and the tracker) the node keeps, beside the survey's logged frames, what the pass needs: the survey's poses, velocities and rangefinder readings as they come (`flight_record.jsonl`) and, when the survey stops, the tracks as the flight leaves them with their digit votes and the local frame's origin (`live_tracks.json`). The pass gives every logged frame to the flight's own pipeline with tiling on, in the order the frames were taken, fed from that record; the 900 s are kept by looking at fewer frames, evenly, never by running over, and 45 s of them are held back for the merge and the list. Merge: a second-pass track within 1.5 m of a live track of the same class is the same marker (place by sightings, votes summed); no live track is dropped or moved onto another marker; a confirmed second-pass track inside the search area that matches nothing is added; the digits are then given out again over all of them by the vote's own rule. The merged list is written as the judges' list is, to a folder the person names, and what changed is printed a line a marker. From the reviews: the record is written by a thread of its own and the tracks when the survey stops likewise, so the node's one thread never waits on the disk; a step of the flight controller's position found in the record moves the replay's tracks as it moved the flight's; the settings of the flight's pipeline that the pass must share (the ground's height below home, the digit reader's confidence, median positions, unique IDs) are kept with the tracks and read by the tool, not given again by hand; and the flag on without the frame log or the tracker is said and left out, where it first stopped the node. | The spec says after landing, tiled, merged with the live tracks, within 900 s, behind a flag until the organisers rule. Outright penalties match decision 18 (a wrong ID must cost more than abstaining). All are settings |

- 2026-11-20 LOC-8 DONE: the weighted vote, `argus_localisation/digit_vote.py`, behind the node flag `features.digit_vote` (with the tracker's and the digit reader's). Each reading adds its ten log-probabilities to the track its box went to, weighted by the marker's size in the crop, the patch's sharpness, how nearly overhead it was seen and the detector's confidence. A track has a digit when its best score beats "nothing can be said" and its second best by odds of 9 to 1. With `digit_ids_unique` (default true) the digits are given out by one Hungarian assignment over the listed tracks and the ten digits, so of two tracks claiming a digit the one with the evidence has it; claims the evidence does not separate are left unknown and listed as contested. The digit goes out in `MarkerTrack`'s own fields. Reader and vote together on drawn 60 px markers, eight sightings each: all ten digits right on last year's plate, the eight answerable ones on this year's marker. Spec audit complete in one round; the flight-safety review's second round had no findings. 12 vote tests, 149 in the package.

The classifier is an ONNX model on the CPU (none shipped: the data hold) or, behind `features.template_digit_classifier` and in the sim only, a stand-in for the sim's marker model. One new setting, `estimator_centering_tolerance_m` (0.20 m in both), says how close to the estimator's track counts as centred, so the live files' 0.5 and 0.8 m for the raw detection are left alone. The sim copy tool makes `sim_package_*_2027.yaml` (four copies now) and gives the delivery's copy the sim's package height. Sim, calm, the live rates and heights with eight of each file's ten flags on: the drop released on its gates 0.026 m from the target, the delivery set down 0.029 m from it (`drop/live_tuning_2027`, `delivery/live_tuning_2027`). On the aircraft neither file builds with a 2027 flag on until the camera mode is calibrated and the airframe measured. 9 sequence tests. `docs/results/2026-11-20-sequences-2027.md`.
- 2026-11-20 CEN-06 DONE: smart re-acquisition. Behind the new mission flag `smart_reacquire` (needs `use_target_estimator`, `centre_on_estimator`), a drop or delivery whose track the estimator calls LOST does not wait its own grace time or climb a metre: it goes to (3 sigma + 2.5 m) / k above the ground over the track's last estimate (2.5 m sideways at most, the rest looked for from higher), holds up to 10 s from arriving for a CONFIRMED track, and then acquires it as in 2026 or fails to the failure policy. The switch is in the base mission's recovery; neither mission's state machine changed. Sim (`drop/reacquire`, a target that cannot be kept below 3 m): four losses, each looked for at once from 5.9 m, confirmed again on arriving, descending again 5 s after LOST (7 s with the 2026 recovery on the same target), then the attempt limit and the failure policy. 18 mission tests, among them the gated drop's 25 s timeout as the way in, and 11 rule tests. flight-guardian: four concerns, three fixed, one for the lead (the look is from under the survey's 7.62 m, as the spec's formula gives); spec-auditor complete after the second round. `docs/results/2026-11-20-smart-reacquire.md`.
- 2026-11-20 CEN-05 DONE: the delivery's soft set-down. Behind the new mission flag `delivery_soft_set_down` (needs `use_target_estimator`, `centre_on_estimator`, `use_height_estimator`), FINAL_SET_DOWN takes the place of the fixed GPS column: the delivery goes on down on the estimator's track, takes a hold when low and centred (0.6 m above the ground, or at the height under which it takes no target), descends at 0.12 m/s, and releases on contact: the rangefinder at the package's height, no vertical speed and the throttle 15% down, together for 0.3 s, with the flight controller's "landed" as the other way in. Then 1 s and the 2026 relaunch. New: `context.throttle()` from `/mavros/vfr_hud` (the plugin and a 20 Hz rate added to the 2027 MAVROS settings and the stream keeper) and `context.rangefinder_range()`; mission key `package_height_m`, without which the sequence does not build. Sim, calm, a real 0.5 kg package: touched at 0.12 m/s (2026: 0.25), release 0.8 s after the legs touched (2.6 s), 2.6 s on the ground (7.5 s), package 0.010 m from the centre (0.165 m); a second scenario takes the hold at the projection floor. 27 mission tests, 18 rule tests. flight-guardian found a blocker (on level ground the first version could not reach its hold with a track) and seven concerns, all fixed, second round without a blocker; spec-auditor complete after the second round. On the aircraft the flag waits on three person steps. `docs/results/2026-11-20-soft-set-down.md`.
- 2026-11-20 CEN-04 DONE: the gated drop. Behind the new mission flag `drop_release_gates` (needs `use_target_estimator`, `centre_on_estimator`, `use_height_estimator`), FINAL_ALIGN takes the place of the fixed GPS column: from the 8 m handoff the drop steers on the estimator's track down to 2.4 m on the rangefinder (3.0 m on the barometer) and releases at once when error 0.10 m, sigma 0.08 m, speed 0.15 m/s, tilt 6°, a track hit within 0.3 s and the height band have held together for 0.5 s. Under 2.0 m it climbs first; after 25 s it looks again once; after a second 25 s it releases within 0.5 m or fails and the sequence moves on. Sim, calm, one flight each: a real 0.5 kg package released from 2.55 m came to rest 0.03 m from the target (0.14 m until the mission was given the place the sim hangs the package, new airframe row `sim_iris_parcel`); a track lost at 3 m released nothing through four recovery attempts; the timeout path ended in a last-resort release 0.04 m off; a handoff under the floor climbed back from 1.90 m and released at 2.29 m. The sim found a log helper that rclpy refuses (it ended the mission; fixed and tested). Two sim checks of earlier features were corrected (projection: whole target in view; estimator: a band only passed through, nothing after the release). 21 mission tests, 6 gate tests. flight-guardian: three concerns, all fixed, second round clean; spec-auditor: complete after the second round. `docs/results/2026-11-20-gated-drop.md`.
- 2026-11-20 CEN-13 PARTIAL: the near-field ring fit. `drone_target_cv/ring_fit.py` finds the bullseye's centre from its rings' red and white edges, on a frame levelled with the vehicle's attitude, where a box around the red is cut by the picture's edge; the new `ring_fit` node (flag `features.ring_fit`, images with a queue of one, below 4 m) publishes it on the detection contract, and with the mission flag `use_ring_fit` the estimator takes it beside the box detector's, weighed by its own 2 px. Rendered views from 1.5 to 4 m, tilted, blurred, noisy and partly out of the picture: 60 of 60 found, median under 0.6 px, worst under 3 px, 16 ms a frame. In Gazebo the 2 m hold in strong wind over the full 1.5 m target held 0.20 m at p95 with no lost track (0.31 m and 30 to 40 losses without it); rings found in 1100 of 1391 frames looked at. Also: a frame now counts once toward confirming a track however many detectors saw it. 35 fit and node tests, 5 tool tests. PARTIAL: the bench check with the printed target and the timing on the Jetson are person steps (`tools/ring_fit_try.py`); the aircraft's launch does not start the node yet (PLT-07). `docs/results/2026-11-20-ring-fit.md`.
- 2026-11-20 G1: PASS at `18e7d05`. Four holds on the estimator with the retuned controller, one seed each: p95 true error 0.11 m (6 m) and 0.10 m (2 m) in moderate wind against 0.20 m; 0.27 m at both heights in strong wind against 0.30 m. The strong-wind margin is 0.03 m, and the 2 m holds are on a 1.0 m target that stays in the tilted camera's view; `docs/results/2026-11-20-gate-G1.md`.
- 2026-11-20 CEN-02 DONE: behind the new mission flag `centring_retune` (needs `centre_on_estimator`), centring uses `centring_controller.py`: the spec's soft deadband 0.03 m, Kp 0.6, speed cap clamp(0.08 h, 0.25, 1.0) m/s and slew 0.5 m/s², plus a 0.5 s lead on the vehicle's velocity that the spec does not have. `tools/cen_loop_sim.py` runs the same class in a simulated loop (gain sweep, the 2026 tunings beside it). In Gazebo the spec's control alone held 0.12 m at p95 in moderate wind and 0.335 m in strong wind, ringing against the vehicle's slow velocity response; with the lead the four wind holds were 0.10 m (moderate, 6 m and 2 m) and 0.27 m (strong, both), inside G1's 0.20 and 0.30 m by a thin margin in strong wind. Gate G1 now has its four flights. Also: the sim's wind fades out on the vehicle below 0.5 m (two strong-wind runs landed and never disarmed), and the 2 m wind holds use a 1.0 m target (a 1.5 m one leaves the tilted camera's view). 11 controller, 8 simulator and 17 new mission tests. `docs/results/2026-11-20-centring-retune.md`.
- 2026-11-20 CEN-01 DONE: behind the new mission flag `centre_on_estimator` (needs `use_target_estimator`), the drop and delivery missions centre on the estimator's bullseye track instead of the raw detection, with no deadband and no low-pass filter, and what they put over the target is the payload's release point (`robot.yaml`'s offset, turned by the vehicle's yaw). A track that may not be descended on is steered toward but never counts as centred, so nothing commits on a remembered point; one approach keeps to one track. Sim, calm: held for 20 s over the target, the true error at p95 was 0.024 m at 6 m and 0.018 m at 2 m (2026 centring: 0.067 and 0.069 m); a release point 0.30 m ahead and 0.10 m left was held 0.019 m from the target with the vehicle 0.32 m away; the delivery touched down 0.01 m off. The drop judge now reports a hold's true error, at the vehicle or a point of it, which gate G1 needs; the trace records the vehicle's true heading. 34 mission tests and 20 new sim tests. flight-guardian found a blocker (commit on a COASTING track), fixed; second round clean. `docs/results/2026-11-20-centring.md`.
- 2026-11-20 CEN-03 PARTIAL: `drone_mission_core/height_estimator.py`, behind the new mission flag `use_height_estimator` (needs `use_frame_time_pose`): `context.height_agl()` gives the rangefinder's height, tilt-corrected, when its readings are within the TFmini's 0.1 to 12 m, fresh, agreeing and taken under 15° of tilt, and the vehicle is under 15° now; otherwise the height above home plus a known ground offset, with `source` and the reason. Three readings in a row out of range, or a reading stuck through 0.2 m of travel, end the rangefinder height at once.
